Merry Christmas, Happy Holidays and a Happy New Year everyone!

This update adds experimental Online Multiplayer to NetherSX2 along with the usual updates!
Thanks to [IamLupo](https://github.com/IamLupo) for adding it to ARMSX2, and [zakilj3](https://www.youtube.com/user/zakilj3) for discovering the same settings work with NetherSX2!

1. Go to your App Settings --> Settings and toggle on Enable DEV9 Ethernet
2. Set API to Sockets, and Device to how you want to connect online with the default being WiFi. Set this to VPN if your phone uses a VPN, and to one of the two SIM DATA options if you want to use your Mobile Data Plan instead
3. That should be enough to get you online using a guide like [this](https://youtu.be/dcOnZzzcbSc?si=WOf01r0Ln5ZVQkpf&t=278) by LogicalMacrochip

releases.body:
# X360 Mobile 0.6.2 Public Hotfix 1

This maintenance release hardens the Vulkan and Android runtime introduced in
0.6.2. It keeps the same public feature line and concentrates on conservative
driver compatibility, reusable caches, memory stability and correct platform
scheduling.

## Vulkan compatibility and cache stability

- Added `vulkan_extended_dynamic_state=auto|static|dynamic` globally and per
  game. `auto` uses the faster Vulkan 1.3 path on capable Qualcomm and Mesa
  drivers, while proprietary Mali and Samsung/Xclipse drivers retain the
  established static path until their exact GPU and driver combination has
  been physically validated.
- Explicit `dynamic` mode still falls back safely when the complete required
  Vulkan functionality is unavailable. PanVK and other Mesa drivers are not
  confused with proprietary drivers from the same GPU vendor.
- Host pipeline descriptions are now isolated between static and dynamic
  modes. Vulkan binary caches are additionally separated by the driver's
  pipeline-cache identity and version, preventing incompatible data from being
  reused after a driver, mode or application update.
- Pipeline-cache writes are atomic and periodical

releases.body:
- **More free memory for demanding games.** The console's memory is one pool shared by the emulated console, the emulator itself and the graphics, and part of it was held without being used. The emulated console's memory, the code caches and a reserve on the system's side now take memory only when they need it. A large open-world game at 2x has about 3.5 GiB free during play instead of 2.2 GiB, at the same frame rate, so a long session runs out of memory far later.

- **Fixed: the multi-second freezes.** A draw whose pipeline was still compiling used to block the renderer with an *unbounded* wait on the compile queue. This release finalizes the 5.0 series.

Emulation accuracy
- New option CPU_START_DELAY staggers the CPU start relative to the beam. Without it, some memory configurations always hit a timing race in Kickstart 1.3’s PAL/NTSC detection (#1029).
- Reinstated the ADF track-length fix that had been dropped by mistake (#1021).

Usability
- Improved auto-warp condition (#1008).
- “Close unsaved instances without asking” now works reliably.
- Choosing the Performance preset no longer wipes the saved collision-detection defaults.

Under the hood
- Public API cleanup
- Detailed API documentation at https://dirkwhoffmann.github.io/vAmiga/docs/index.html

Enhancements: 
- Moira now emulates the 68020 instruction cache.

Bug fixes:
- Improved AGA support (#999, #1003, #1004, #1009, #1011, #1012, #1013).

New features: 
- AGA support

# Release Notes

## Enhancements

- The floppy disk API now supports disk images stored in memory buffers (#992)
- Added proper gamma correction to the palette builders (#998)
- Replaced the 4096-entry palette lookup table with a smaller table based on an affine transformation, paving the way for AGA support.

## Bug Fixes

- Fixed a bug that caused the server launch daemon to fire every cycle (#990)
- Fixed a bug that prevented preferences from loading correctly (#995)
- Added guard checks for potential Swift `nil` values
- Fixed a bug in the **Export to…** menu (#989)
- Reverted pull request #837 (#984)

Ending the beta phase, as no severe bugs have been reported recently.

Bug fixes:
- Fixed an issue that prevented folders from being imported as hard drives (#975)

releases.name: xbased 1.0.47
releases.body:
## 1.0.47 (2026-11)

### New
- Stick anti dead zone, in Settings, Controls, Stick range, and for each
  game in its own Controls. Many Xbox games ignore the first part of a
  stick's travel themselves (they were made for the original controller's
  loose sticks), so even with the dead zone at 0 a small push does
  nothing. In Chicago Enforcer, for example, the view doesn't turn at all
  until the stick is about a third of the way over. The anti dead zone
  makes the smallest push past the dead zone start at that amount, so
  the game reacts straight away. Both stick boxes on the Stick range
  screen draw it as a red disc, next to the dead zone's grey ring.
- A game's Controls now have its own sticks (dead zone, anti dead zone,
  range, shape) and triggers, so each game can be set apart from the
  global settings. Thanks to crashmidnick25 for the report (#84).

releases.name: xbased 1.0.46
releases.body:
## 1.0.46 (2026-11)

### Fixes
- Less audio stutter on Linux in games with a lot of sound going on,
  like Forza Motorsport's races. The emulated sound chip's voices were
  split between the audio thread and a helper thread, and on Linux
  waking the helper and waiting for it 1500 times a second cost more
  than the work it took over. In a Forza race the audio thread was busy
  about three times as much on Linux as on Windows on the same machine,
  and on slower laptops it couldn't keep up. On Linux the audio thread
  now does the voices itself, which takes it from around 20% busy to
  around 7% in that race. Windows keeps the helper, which pays off
  there. Thanks to saultsomy-jpg for the report and the detailed log
  (#82).

releases.name: xbased 1.0.45
releases.body:
## 1.0.45 (2026-11)

### Fixes
- Chicago Enforcer no longer freezes when starting a new game. Its
  loading screen works with events it opens by name, and the emulator
  had no way to open an object by name, so it stopped right there. Named
  events, semaphores and mutants are now supported, and a name goes away
  with the last handle to it, as on the console, since the next loading
  screen waits for exactly that. The game now gets through both loads
  of the first chapter and plays. Thanks to P1Login for the report (#56).

releases.name: xbased 1.0.44
releases.body:
## 1.0.44 (2026-11)

### Fixes
- The updater on Windows no longer gives up on an update that unpacked
  fine. It unpacks the new version with Windows' own tar, and on some
  Windows 10 machines tar reported an error even though every file came
  out right, so the updater stopped and opened the releases page
  instead. Now, when tar reports an error, the updater checks every
  file of the package against the download (its name and size) and
  carries on if they're all there. Thanks to shadowflash for the report
  (#76).

releases.name: xbased 1.0.43
releases.body:
## 1.0.43 (2026-11)

### Fixes
- Crimson Skies: High Road to Revenge no longer goes back to the
  dashboard as it starts. Some games check that the disc is an original
  by reading its security sector, which lives in a part of the disc that
  disc images don't include, and the emulator handed back zeros. The
  emulated DVD drive now makes a security sector that passes the game's
  check (the right time stamp and checksum, signed with a key of
  xbased's own, which the emulated console uses as its public key). The
  game now boots and plays. Thanks to BlueDragon992 for the report (#80).

## Highlights

- **Disk images are kept unmodified with a save directory.** With `-saveDir`, what the software writes goes to an overlay file there and the image is only read. Overlays store only the tracks or blocks written and are tied to a checksum of their image. This also makes writable the disks that could not be written before: inside a zip or gzip, loaded from a URL, or embedded in the executable.
- **DOS 3.3 boots in five seconds.** The Disk II motor keeps turning for about a second after the drive is turned off, like the 556 timer of the real controller, and the data latch no longer reads the same nibble twice. DOS no longer waits for the motor on every access: a DOS 3.3 boot takes 5.4 million cycles instead of 36 million.
- **A libretro core** runs izapple2 inside RetroArch and the other libretro frontends, with diskette swapping from M3U playlists and saves as overlays. ## Banana Native v0.1.4

Install over v0.1.3: saves, packs and settings are kept. No shader update is needed.

- **In-app updates.** From this version on, the app checks this page when it starts and offers new releases in a popup (Update or Later). It downloads the APK from this page and checks it before Android asks you to install it. Settings › Check for updates checks right away.
- **`0400C3F00006E000`: Prepare no longer stops at "rewriting the game code" (#20).** That step now needs about a fifth of the memory (0.5 GB instead of about 3 GB), so it finishes on phones with other apps open. If Prepare stopped for you, tap Retry.
- **No more false "Pack from other tools" chip** on packs this app made. Packs made by earlier versions count as current; nothing has to be prepared again.

Needs Android 13+, a Snapdragon (Adreno) phone with 12 GB of RAM or more, and your own dump. Experimental: back up your saves. Download only from this page. No games, keys or shaders are included. GPL-3.0-or-later.

releases.name: Ryujinx-Nextendo 1.10.2
releases.body:
## Mario Kart 8 Deluxe online fixed (2306-0502)
- 1.10.0 started deferring every Bsd poll with a finite timeout. That broke the NEX connection of Mario Kart 8 Deluxe, which failed with error 2306-0502. MK8's ordinary NEX polls now use the blocking path again, as in 1.9.9; eventfd polls and the finite-timeout optimization of other games (Portal 2 and others) are unchanged (#75)

## New online games
- SpeedRunners 2: Nextendo routes scoped to the game, and a TLS peer reset during the handshake is now returned to the game as an SSL error instead of stopping the emulator (#79)
- Just Dance 2022: Nextendo routes, exact-build TLS trust patch with native certificate verification kept on, and blocking UDP receives no longer hold the shared socket thread (#74)
- Ultimate Chicken Horse 1.13.13.765: online support (#68)
- Guilty Gear Strive: online services redirected to Nextendo (#77)
- Nintendo Switch Online Classics: versions set for NES, SNES, Game Boy, Game Boy Advance, Nintendo 64 and SEGA Genesis, plus a Windows JIT fix (#69)

## Other fixes
- Steam Deck: touchscreen, rumble and gyro input (#76)
- NPLN online patches are loaded from the signed patch catalog (#73)
- nim: the IShopServic

## Friends
- The friend list filter of a game (online, same game, favorites) is now applied before the list is cut to the game's buffer, so a game asking for friends in the same game gets them.
- A friend is "in the same game" only when their presence names the game you are playing.
- The friend panel and the "Friend online" notification show the name of the game, using the name sent by the Nextendo server when the title is unknown locally.
- Splatoon 3 and Portal 2 added to the game name table.

## Also in this version (from 1.10.0)
- Portal 2: online menus and the co-op lobby run at full speed, crash after a failed join fixed, 1.0.3 required online.
- Network: a socket wait with a time limit no longer blocks the other network calls of the game.
- Game version table: Minecraft 1.0.17 and Portal 2 1.0.3.

## Update
- The built-in updater offers this version (Help > Check for Updates, or System Update in the HOME Menu) and keeps your portable folder: keys, saves and account stay in place.
